news.title: Construction et bureaucratie, interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans et le pour et le contre de l'Ozempic
news.podcast_name: La revue de presse de Paul Arcand
news.summary: À l'occasion de sa revue de presse, mardi matin, Paul Arcand aborde la bureaucratie écrasante et les délais interminables pour obtenir un permis de construction ou de rénovation à Montréal, à Laval et au Québec en général.  Selon un rapport de l'Institut de Développement Urbain du Québec, les délais d'attribution ont pratiquement doublé depuis 2017 en raison de la multiplication des critères et des étapes bureaucratiques, enregistrant une hausse moyenne de 135% à Laval, Québec et Montréal.  À Montréal, 20% des permis de construction prennent près d'un an à obtenir, tandis que dans l'arrondissement de Ville-Marie, il faut compter en moyenne 560 jours pour les projets résidentiels de quatre à 11 logements.  Ces délais entraînent des coûts supplémentaires majeurs, évalués à 700 000$ de plus pour un projet de 10 millions de dollars retardé d'un an.  Autres sujets traités:   Ottawa va interdire les réseaux sociaux aux moins de 16 ans; La garde à vue de Patrick Bruel prolongée de 24 heures; Ozempic: le pour et le contre.    Voir https://www.cogecomedia.com/vie-privee pour notre politique de vie privée

news.summary: A few months ago, the Government said New Zealanders could end up helping fund a new LNG import terminal through their power bills. politics.summary: A fistfight erupts in Taiwan's parliament. Punches fly as two rivals find themselves at the centre of the chaos. arts.summary: Seven years ago last Tuesday, The Emerald podcast was born. This episode reflects on the journey of the podcast so far and gives hints of what's to come, all through the prism of the number 7, which is — to say the least — a mythically important number. The myths often iterate in cycles and families of seven—seven swans, seven dwarves, seven ravens, and seven gates of the underworld. In many traditions, seven represents the completion of a cycle and the beginning of a new one. In Ayurveda, in order for something to be fully embodied, it must pass through seven dhatus, or tissue layers. In many traditions, initiates pass through a journey of seven stages. This recurring 'journey through seven' is not just arbitrary, it is a reflection of nature itself, which often repeats in cycles of seven. The ancients saw seven at play in the architecture of the cosmos, in the musical scales and the spectrum of light and in a world that they saw as expressing through seven cosmic layers. The vision of seven as a number of threshold, passage, and reconnection can be understood through the numerical and geometric attributes of seven itself, which displays strange characteristics not found in any other number. Featuring Nivedita Gunturi singing the seven-note scale progressions of Hindustani and Carnatic music, and excerpts of beloved stories of seven, this episode is a celebration of seven years of The Emerald, and a preparation for what's to come.  Support the show

arts.summary: For decades starting in the 1940s, Ebony was one of the only magazines created by Black people that spoke directly to Black people. Now it’s part of the National Museum of African American History and Culture’s permanent collection. arts.title: Joan Snyder
arts.summary: TODAY on the GWA Podcast is the esteemed painter Joan Snyder. Hailed for her large-scale gestural canvases that pulsate with colour, line and text, and are often layered with, buried in, or imploded with images of flowers, faces, or bodies, Snyder's all-encompassing works are nothing but electric. Sometimes large scale, with brushstrokes that populate the canvas like gemstones or musical scores with a whole range of keys: look at Snyder's work for a while, and it's like whole worlds emerge. Simultaneously soft but violent, beautiful yet aggressive, her works can evoke every season of emotion, just as she once wrote in her journal in 1972: "The strokes in my painting speak of my life and experiences. They are sometimes soft, they sometimes laugh, and are often violent. They bleed and cry. I speak of love and anguish, of fear, and mostly of hope."  Born in 1940, Snyder came to art not straight away, but by chance during her studies at Rutgers University, when she was studying sociology in preparation for a career in social work. But it was under the mentorship of Billy Prichard that she pivoted to art, showing just how important teachers can be. Today we meet Joan in her Brooklyn studio, where she remains one of the legendary artists of her time. A recipient of a MacArthur Fellowship and an American Academy of Arts and Letters Award, and in museum collections all over the world, Snyder, at 85 – nearly 86 – is painting more than ever and this summer, will take to Paris for her upcoming show, Earthsongs at Thaddaeus Ropac Paris, and I cannot wait to find out more. arts.summary: – 本节目由GIADA出品 – 【本期制作人】JustPod 【本期嘉宾】 蔡皋，艺术家、绘本画家 陈鲁豫，媒体人、主持人 【本期节目介绍】 岩中花述第九季第三期节目，鲁豫在刚下过雨的春日清晨，与绘本画家蔡皋一同点石成「绿」。 今时已拐入8字头，她说，每一个日子都是新的，我每天享受欣欣不已的「受激」状态，等着那新鲜事物进来，但昨天也不是消失了，而是沉淀进生活的画布，晕染、覆盖，一天有一天的斑驳，教人直觉新意满满。 当画卷般的昨天徐徐展开，我们也借着这斑驳的画意望进一个女人的生命： 画画打小就喜欢着，而时代变动随意摆弄个人命运，她进入县文化馆一年、就被调往偏僻乡下，度过7年教学与劳作的漫长光阴，最好的年纪看似是浪费了，但凭着「我喜欢，我选择」的强大主体性，她硬是将绘画拽回身边，画玻璃、做木工是创作，主席像、黑板报是练笔，最普通的生活也溢满艺术，她终究绕回了原本的道路。 那贫苦是一种禁锢，却也让她理解土地、爱上种植、敬畏生命，不仅孕育出属于她的「桃花源」，也积淀出她对美的认识，祖辈曾有的富丽大宅倒塌了不要紧，只要「插上我的映山红」就很好。 她说「我像晚熟的水稻」，36岁才迈入绘本的新世界，55岁退休才真正觉得解放，迎来了创作的巅峰期。人总会等到条件成熟，好比从岩石缝隙里狠扎下根去的植物，你不知道当它吸饱了水分，能长出什么样的倔强来。 就像，一个十分平常的日子，她在那座屋顶花园，毫无预备地看到不知从何处来的虞美人开了花——哦，这不也是它的条件到了吗？ 【内容提要】 Part 1 人生如画卷，日日重复而新 04:31 「皋」意为水边高地，她也如草本、与水相伴而生 06:31 始终以今日的颜色装点昨日的画卷，一日便有一日的新鲜 10:37 一本书是一棵树的代价，创作不妨沉淀久些、才留得住这张纸 Part 2 创作，本就能在任何条件下生发 13:38 7年乡村女教师，流泪下乡、却也悟出了自然的禅意 18:06 「拿着画笔的时候，我好幸福，我希望幸福不要跑了」 21:08 生活必须兼具务实，但艺术能让人在困顿中品尝奶酪 24:37 从未停止画画，主席像、宣传画、黑板报都是练笔的方式 28:21 就凭「我喜欢，我选择」，艰难无法将创作与「我」剥离 33:02 心里有一颗理想的种子，就能从贫瘠的岩缝开出花朵 Part 3 退休后的大解放，把真实种出来 38:18 艺术之外，在琐碎中、在病痛中，找到磨合与自愈的方法 43:15 外婆、妈妈与我，三代女性在各自的时代中活出个性 59:27 普通人的书写更接近生活本身，历史需要平民记录的真实 01:06:50 观察植物也是关照自己，文字也能从「花园」里种出来 01:16:14 我太爱我的生活了，像玉兰一样倔强、芬芳，继续开很久 – 主题曲 – Taine），法国著名的文艺理论家和史学家，历史文化学派的奠基者和领袖人物，受斯宾诺莎、黑格尔哲学影响，丹纳在文学艺术研究中提出一种决定论，即“种族-环境-时代”三因素，代表作《艺术哲学》等 松居直（まつい ただし），日本编辑、出版人、儿童文学家，被誉为“日本图画书之父”，著有《我的图画书论》《幸福的种子》等书，倡导“图画书是大人读给孩子听的书”的亲子阅读理念 「三五之夜，明月半墙，桂影斑驳，风移影动，珊珊可爱」，出自明代归有光的《项脊轩志》 蔡皋读的童谣原文：「麻雀生蛋粒粒滚，叫声哥哥去买粉。买得粉来不会搽，又说哥哥不买麻。买得麻来不会绩，又说哥哥不买笔。买得笔来不会削，又说哥哥不买刀。买得刀来不会磨，又说哥哥不买鹅。买得鹅来不敢杀，又说哥哥不买鸭。买得鸭来不会钳，又说哥哥不买田。买得田来不会作，又说哥哥不洗脚。洗了脚，把田作，作了田，把毛钳；钳了毛，把鹅杀；杀了鹅，把刀磨；磨了刀，把笔削；削了笔，把麻绩；绩了麻，把粉搽；搽了粉，麻雀生蛋粒粒滚。」 「岩中花述」同名图书《岩中花述》（全四册）已经正式上市啦！ 书中收录了由鲁豫老师参与主持的第3-6季中34位嘉宾的对谈内容，并根据不同的话题维度，分为了4本书出版：《我决定，要活得很久》《她们重新发明知识》《不退场的勇气》《这是我修改世界的方式》。 希望我们都能在嘈杂、偏见的声音中，活到「后来」！ arts.title: Anne Fadiman on Essays, Personal and Historical
arts.podcast_name: The World in Time / Lapham’s Quarterly
arts.summary: “An 1833 review of the only book of poetry Hartley Coleridge published in his lifetime praised the verse for embodying ‘no trivial inheritance of his father's genius,’ but also observed, ‘It is an old saying that the oakling withers beneath the shadow of the oak.’ I have long been interested in what makes some oaklings thrive and others wither, because, in a minor way, I’m an oakling myself. My father was a critic and an essayist. My mother was a war correspondent. The upside of this print-smudged parentage was that I was raised in a home with seven thousand books, plenty of literary conversation, and empirical evidence that writing was something you could actually do for a living."   This week on the podcast, Donovan Hohn speaks with essayist Anne Fadiman about the history of the essay since Montaigne and the art of making essays out of history; about teaching essay-writing to college students; and about what Virginia Woolf called “the Common Reader.” The conversation addresses the title essay—about a pet frog named Bunky—of Fadiman’s new collection, Frog and Other Essays, but Hohn and Fadiman spend the most time with two other essays—one that originally appeared in the Family issue of Lapham’s Quarterly, on poet and essayist Hartley Coleridge, who grew up in the shadow of his famous father, Samuel Taylor, and one first published in the Harvard Review, about the South Polar Times, a magazine whose editors, contributors, and original readers were all members of the polar expeditions led by Robert Falcon Scott.
